candidates.name: Wes Moore
candidates.now: Governor of Maryland (since 2023)
candidates.background: Governor since 2023 and the first Black governor in Maryland history; Army veteran (captain, 82nd Airborne, deployed to Afghanistan), Rhodes Scholar, and former CEO of the Robin Hood Foundation anti-poverty group. Beat Dan Cox roughly 65-32 in 2022 and won renomination June 23 with about 88% of the Democratic primary vote. Widely discussed as a potential 2028 presidential candidate.
priorities: Lower costs and raise wages for working families
Fully fund the Blueprint for Maryland's Future education plan
100% clean energy by 2035

cost.label: Signed the Fair Wage Act accelerating the $15 minimum wage and allocated $218M to help providers absorb it (Wikipedia)

health.label: 'Healthcare is a basic right that every Marylander deserves'; behavioral-health coverage, protect community health centers (Ballotpedia)

housing.label: Housing Expansion and Affordability Act plus tenant protections, right to counsel in evictions, and an order to clear 5,000 vacant Baltimore homes (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Signed the Maryland Values Act barring immigration enforcement at sensitive locations; declined to send the Guard to the border; condemned the Abrego Garcia deportation (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Mixed: signed 2025 budget raising $1B+ via new brackets on the wealthy and a 2% capital gains surcharge, but paired with $2.5B in spending cuts after proposing corporate rate cuts (Wikipedia)

climate.label: 100% carbon-free electricity by 2035 and net-zero by 2045; POWER Act targets 8.5 GW of offshore wind by 2031 (Wikipedia)

education.label: Funds the Blueprint public-school plan ($500M first budget) while cutting the BOOST voucher program with intent to phase it out (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Leans prevention: community violence-intervention funding and the Youth Charging Reform Act, alongside tougher juvenile probation measures and police data-platform funding (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Backed the constitutional abortion-rights amendment, a $25M abortion access fund, mifepristone stockpiles, and a 2026 emergency-abortion hospital mandate (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Signed the Maryland Voting Rights Act (SB 255) banning racially discriminatory local voting systems and 'removing barriers to the ballot box' (NAACP LDF)

sources.label: Maryland State Board of Elections: general candidate list

candidates.name: Dan Cox
candidates.now: Attorney, The Cox Law Center
candidates.background: Constitutional lawyer and former state delegate (2019-2023) from Frederick County; father of ten. The 2022 Republican nominee for governor, he lost to Wes Moore roughly 65-32, then won the June 23, 2026 primary with 45% over Ed Hale Sr.'s 36% for a rematch. Endorsed by President Trump in his 2022 run.
priorities: Reduce and eliminate taxes and fees
Border security and fighting fentanyl trafficking
Restore police funding and public safety

cost.label: Pledges to 'reduce and eliminate taxes and fees' and to 'limit, cap, and, where possible, eliminate property taxes' to make Maryland more affordable (campaign site)

housing.label: Mixed: down-payment assistance and first-time homebuyer tax credits alongside cutting 'building costs and permitting burdens' (campaign site)

immigration.label: Opposes sanctuary policies; backs E-verify enforcement, 'Remain in Mexico', and ending catch-and-release (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: 'Lower taxes, bigger paychecks': reduce property taxes and 'Reduce Inflation by Suspending the Gas Tax' (Ballotpedia)

climate.label: 'Unleash domestic energy resources' and 'eliminate the socialist Green New Deal' (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Expand charter schools, vouchers, and tax credits; opposes CRT and 'gender ideology' in curricula (Ballotpedia)

safety.label: 'Double pay' for police officers, restore 'full quasi-immunity', opposes defunding the police (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: Defends 'the right to all human life, from conception to natural death' (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: 'Election integrity' via voter ID and hand-counted paper ballots; called for audits of the 2020 election (Ballotpedia)

health.label: Backs 'expanding healthcare choice, transparency, and affordability' and 'increased competition in the health insurance market' (Ballotpedia)

controversies.label: Arranged buses to the Jan 6, 2021 'Save America March' and tweeted 'Pence is a traitor' during the riot; continuously promoted disproven 2020 fraud claims (Wikipedia)
Introduced articles of impeachment against Gov. Larry Hogan over pandemic policies, rejected unanimously; filed unsuccessful suits against mail-in ballot counting (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Andrew P Harris
candidates.now: U.S. Representative for Maryland's 1st Congressional District (since 2011)
candidates.background: Anesthesiologist (Johns Hopkins M.D.) first elected in 2010 and serving since 2011, now the dean of Maryland's House delegation and a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee. Drew national attention for downplaying the Jan 6, 2021 Capitol attack and promoting unproven 2020 election fraud claims. Won the June 23, 2026 Republican primary with about 80 percent and faces Democrat Dan Schwartz in November.
priorities: Border security and opposing pathways to citizenship
Cutting taxes and reducing federal spending
Restricting abortion and defending pro-life policy

health.label: Called the ACA a 'government takeover of health care', voted for the 2017 American Health Care Act repeal effort, and backed Medicaid work requirements for able-bodied adults (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Voted yes on the Laken Riley Act (S.5) requiring detention of undocumented immigrants accused of theft and related crimes, Jan 22, 2025, roll call 23 (Clerk, U.S. House)

taxes.label: Voted yes on H.R.1, the 2025 tax and budget reconciliation law making the 2017 tax cuts permanent, Jul 3, 2025, roll call 190 (Clerk, U.S. House)

climate.label: Amended 2017 appropriations legislation to ban federal funding for offshore wind farms near the Maryland coast and advocated restarting the Keystone pipeline plus more gas and coal production (Wikipedia)

education.label: Introduced legislation in 2001 creating a statewide, state-funded scholarship program for students to attend private schools (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Voted against a two-year moratorium on death penalty sentences in 2003 (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Cosponsored the Life at Conception Act banning abortion without exceptions and celebrated the Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Voted yes on the SAVE Act (H.R.22) requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, Apr 10, 2025, roll call 102 (Clerk, U.S. House)

candidates.name: John Anthony Jr. Olszewski
candidates.now: U.S. Representative for Maryland's 2nd Congressional District (since 2025); former Baltimore County Executive
candidates.background: Former Baltimore County Executive (2018-2024) elected to Congress in 2024 after Dutch Ruppersberger's retirement. As county executive he pushed affordable-housing mandates, a $70 million teacher-pay and free-community-college package, and a police reform law after George Floyd's murder. Seeks re-election against Republican Dave Wallace in a rematch of the 2024 race.
priorities: Codify Roe v. Wade and expand affordable housing
Protect Medicaid and oppose the 2025 GOP tax and budget law
Raise wages and expand renewable energy

cost.label: Testified in 2019 supporting a bill raising Maryland's minimum wage to $15 an hour by 2026 and backed prevailing-wage requirements for county workers (Wikipedia)

health.label: Said as a 2024 candidate he would support 'any effort to expand health care' that was passable in Congress and signed a pledge to extend Inflation Reduction Act health subsidies (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Signed a December 2024 executive order requiring developers receiving county financial support to set aside at least 20 percent of units as affordable housing, and championed a source-of-income anti-discrimination law for tenants (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Voted no on the Laken Riley Act (S.5), saying it would 'endanger harmless children and divert billions of dollars away from securing the border', Jan 22, 2025, roll call 23 (Clerk, U.S. House)

taxes.label: Voted no on the 2025 GOP tax bill, saying it 'funds tax cuts for the wealthy by increasing costs for the middle class' and adds more than $3 trillion to the debt (press release)

climate.label: Set a goal in April 2021 of using 100 percent renewable energy for Baltimore County government operations by 2026 (Wikipedia)

education.label: Proposed $70 million in April 2023 toward increasing teacher salaries and expanding the county's free community college program, unanimously approved by the County Council (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Introduced legislation in September 2020 banning police chokeholds, protecting police whistleblowers, and requiring officers to intervene against excessive force, which became law (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Condemned the Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade and, as a 2024 congressional candidate, supported 'codifying Roe v. Wade on the federal level' (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Voted no on the SAVE Act (H.R.22) requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, Apr 10, 2025, roll call 102 (Clerk, U.S. House)
